headline: Microsoft lays off 268 Xbox staff as part of major business reset
summary: Ninja Theory faces potential closure as Microsoft continues its significant gaming restructure, impacting studios and franchises.
details: Microsoft has laid off approximately 268 employees across its Xbox division, continuing a significant restructure of its gaming business. This follows earlier layoffs in July that impacted 1,600 employees, which Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described as the most substantial restructure in Xbox history.

The current layoffs are part of a broader plan to cut 3,200 roles within Microsoft's 2027 financial year, which concludes in June 2027. Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty confirmed the roles eliminated are across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and management layers.

As part of the restructuring, Microsoft is also selling off four Xbox studios. While Double Fine and Compulsion Games have already become independent, deals to sell Ninja Theory fell through. Microsoft is now entering a consultation period for the potential closure of Ninja Theory, unless a new buyer is found.

The future of Undead Labs is also in flux, with its sale reportedly proceeding similarly to Compulsion and Double Fine. Consultations are ongoing regarding Arkane Studios and the Blade game, in compliance with French labor laws, with discussions expected to continue until year-end.

In a significant shift, Activision will now assume responsibility for the Halo franchise. Additionally, Sea of Thieves and World's Edge, the studio behind Age of Empires, will also be managed by Activision as part of this extensive Xbox shake-up.

The future of Undead Labs is also in flux, with its sale reportedly proceeding similarly to Compulsion and Double Fine. Consultations are ongoing regarding Arkane Studios and the Blade game, in compliance with French labor laws, with discussions expected to continue until year-end.
